Re-compute of md5 for large files.
**Please provide information about your setup**
DVC v0.40.1, installed via Pipenv on Ubuntu 16.

dvc add data

dvc status

dvc status

dvc push

rm -rf data
rm -rf .dvc/cache

dvc status

dvc pull

dvc status

dvc status

entries.author: teacher
entries.content: Root cause: during checkout (e.g. as part of `dvc pull`), `_checkout_file` and `_checkout_dir` in `dvc/remote/base.py` only called `state.save_link()` but never `state.save()` for the checked-out path, unlike `_save_file`/`_save_dir` used by `dvc add` which save both path and cache checksums. As a result, the checked-out file had no entry in the state database, so the first `dvc status`/`checkout` after a pull found no matching state record and recomputed the full md5 — very expensive for large files (and the checkout itself also triggered a recompute of the freshly downloaded cache file). Fix: call `self.state.save(path_info, checksum)` after linking in both `_checkout_file` and `_checkout_dir`, recording the checksum keyed by the new file's inode/mtime/size. Verified via the issue's repro (status after pull now performs zero md5 computations, for both file and directory outputs) and the existing test suite shows no new failures.
